questions.question: What happens to the energy when a fuel is burned?
options: It transfers energy by cooling down the surroundings.
It transfers energy by heating its surroundings.
It destroys energy so that it is lost forever.
It stores energy within the fuel as physical mass.

questions.question: How can the amount of energy transferred by different fuels be compared in a school laboratory?
options: By measuring the mass of the fuel before it is made.
By measuring the light intensity of the flame using a prism.
By heating water in a boiling tube and measuring the temperature change.
By comparing the color of the smoke produced.

questions.question: When comparing the energy transferred by different fuels, which variable must be kept constant regarding the fuel?
options: The volume of the fuel container.
The chemical formula of the fuel.
The mass of the fuel used for each measurement.
The colour of the fuel.

questions.question: To ensure a fair comparison of energy transferred by different fuels, what must be kept the same for the water being heated?
options: Only its initial temperature, while its volume can vary.
Only its volume, while its initial temperature can vary.
Both its initial temperature and its volume.
Neither its temperature nor its volume needs to be controlled.

questions.question: How do state changes appear on a cooling curve graph?
options: As steep vertical drops in temperature.
As flat, horizontal plateaus.
As steady, diagonal lines sloping upwards.
As sharp, fluctuating spikes.

questions.question: What happens to the energy and state of a substance as it cools down?
options: It absorbs energy from the surroundings and may melt or boil.
It transfers energy into the surroundings by heating and it may condense or freeze.
It keeps its energy constant and always remains in the gas state.
It transfers energy to the surroundings and always sublimates.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key observation during an exothermic chemical reaction?
options: The temperature of the surroundings decreases.
The temperature of the surroundings increases.
The temperature of the surroundings remains completely unchanged.
The substance instantly freezes.

questions.question: What temperature change is observed in the surroundings during an endothermic chemical reaction?
options: A decrease in temperature.
An increase in temperature.
No change in temperature.
The temperature rises to boiling point immediately.

questions.question: In terms of energy transfer, how does an exothermic reaction behave?
options: It transfers energy from the surroundings to the reactants.
It transfers energy from the reactants to the surroundings.
It does not transfer any energy to or from the surroundings.
It destroys energy within the chemical bonds.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the energy transfer in an endothermic reaction?
options: Energy is transferred from the surroundings to the products.
Energy is transferred from the products to the surroundings.
Energy is created within the products without any transfer.
Energy is transferred from the reactants directly to the air as light only.

questions.question: Which of the following processes are classified as endothermic changes of state?
options: Condensing and freezing.
Melting, evaporation, and boiling.
Freezing and melting.
Condensing and boiling.

questions.question: Why are condensing and freezing classified as exothermic changes?
options: They require continuous heating to occur.
They transfer energy out to the surroundings.
They absorb energy from the surroundings.
They increase the temperature of the substance itself.

questions.question: From which resources is over half of the electricity in the UK generated?
options: Coal, oil, and natural gas.
Nuclear power and geothermal energy.
The Sun, wind, and falling water.
Biomass and waste incineration.

questions.question: Which fossil fuel is no longer used in UK power stations to generate electricity?
options: Natural gas
Oil
Coal
Biomass

questions.question: Why will renewable energy resources not run out?
options: They are stored in infinite underground reservoirs.
They are replenished more quickly than we use them up.
They do not transfer any energy when used.
They are created by chemical reactions in power stations.

questions.question: How do solar panels generate electricity differently from wind turbines?
options: They use moving steam to spin a generator.
They burn fuels directly to release electrical energy.
They produce electricity without using electric generators.
They rely on falling water to spin internal coils.
